title: Signature Memory Lineage Ledger
description: Signature edition: every memory write is lineage-stamped — which agent learned it, from what observation, in which session — forming an unbroken chain from fact to source. When a memory proves wrong, the ledger traces it to the exact observation that created it. This is a Signature original method.
method: Each write stores (fact, source observation hash, agent id, session id); corrections append supersede links rather than deleting, preserving the full belief history.
usage: Enable lineage on all writes; audit memories by tracing to sources before acting on old facts.

title: Signature MemGPT virtual context management
description: Signature edition: MemGPT treats the LLM context window like an OS treats RAM: a memory hierarchy with main context (working set), recall storage (full history), and archival storage (long-term facts), managed by the model itself via function calls. The agent pages memories in and out, edits its own long-term store, and never 'forgets' — it archives.
method: The model calls memory functions (archival insert/search, recall search); the runtime enforces token budgets, paging content between tiers on demand.
usage: Define the archival schema up front; let the agent manage paging; audit archival writes for quality.

demo.code:
archival = {}
archival['user_pref'] = 'likes concise answers'
print('archival write:', archival)
print('later recall: agent searches archival -> finds preference')

title: Signature Working-memory scratchpad with tools
description: Signature edition: The scratchpad is the agent's desk: a structured working area (current goal, hypotheses, plan steps, open questions) rewritten each turn, separate from the raw transcript. It keeps long tasks coherent by making the agent's current mental state explicit and inspectable instead of buried in chat history.
method: Maintain a scratchpad object (goal, plan[], hypotheses, blockers); the model updates it each turn via a structured call; tools read/write designated sections.
usage: Keep the scratchpad small and current; archive completed plans to episodic memory; never let it grow unbounded.

demo.code:
pad = {'goal': 'fix deploy', 'plan': ['read logs', 'patch config'], 'blockers': []}
print('scratchpad:', pad)
pad['plan'].append('redeploy')
print('updated plan:', pad['plan'])

title: Signature Salience-scored memory writes
description: Signature edition: Writing everything to long-term memory drowns signal in noise. Salience scoring has the agent rate each observation's future usefulness (user preferences: high; transient tool output: low) and only persists above-threshold items, keeping the memory store dense with things worth remembering.
method: Score each candidate write 0-1 on predicted future utility; persist above threshold; decay scores over time so stale facts fade unless reinforced.
usage: Calibrate the threshold on real sessions: too high loses preferences, too low floods the store.

demo.code:
cands = [('user name is Manon', 0.95), ('temp file listed', 0.1)]
kept = [c for c, s in cands if s >= 0.5]
print('persisted:', kept, '| dropped: temp file listed')

title: Signature Memory consolidation during idle
description: Signature edition: Like sleep for brains: when the agent is idle, a background process replays recent episodes, merges duplicates, extracts durable facts, and prunes noise. Consolidation turns a pile of raw episodes into a clean, queryable long-term store without spending foreground tokens.
method: Idle trigger -> replay recent episodes -> deduplicate -> extract facts to semantic store -> prune raw episodes -> update indexes.
usage: Run consolidation on a schedule; keep raw episodes for a retention window in case consolidation errs.

demo.code:
episodes = ['user likes tea', 'user likes tea (again)', 'deploy at 3pm']
unique = list(dict.fromkeys(episodes))
print('consolidated', len(episodes), '->', len(unique), 'episodes; facts extracted to semantic store')

title: Signature Cross-agent shared memory bus
description: Signature edition: In multi-agent systems, a shared memory bus lets agents publish findings and subscribe to topics instead of passing everything through messages. One agent's discovered fact becomes everyone's recallable memory, with provenance tracking so consumers know who learned what.
method: Publish/subscribe topics on a shared store; writes carry agent id and timestamp; subscribers get notified; provenance rides on every entry.
usage: Namespace topics per task; set write permissions per agent role; expire transient findings.

title: Signature SQLite session journal
description: Signature edition: The humble durable option: every agent step appends to a local SQLite journal (timestamp, action, observation, tokens). Sessions resume by replaying the journal; analytics query it with SQL; nothing depends on a vector DB being up. Simple, inspectable, and effectively free.
method: Append-only events table; session id per run; resume replays events into context; SQL for analytics and debugging.
usage: Journal everything; build resume and analytics on top; add vector search later if recall quality demands it.

demo.code:
import sqlite3
c = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
c.execute('CREATE TABLE events(ts TEXT, kind TEXT, payload TEXT)')
c.execute("INSERT INTO events VALUES ('10:01','note','user likes tea')")
print('journal rows:', c.execute('SELECT * FROM events').fetchall())

title: Signature Summarization compaction
description: Signature edition: When context fills, a summarizer compresses the oldest turns into a dense summary and the conversation continues with summary + recent turns. Done well (hierarchical, entity-preserving), compaction lets sessions run indefinitely; done badly it silently drops the one fact that mattered.
method: On token threshold: summarize oldest N turns preserving entities, decisions, and open loops; replace with the summary; keep a summary-of-summaries chain for very long sessions.
usage: Test compaction on your longest real sessions; pin critical facts (user name, goals) outside the compacted region.

demo.code:
turns = ['user: my dog is Rex', 'agent: noted', 'user: remind me friday']
summary = 'User has dog Rex; wants Friday reminder.'
print('compacted', len(turns), 'turns ->', repr(summary))

title: Signature Knowledge-graph entity memory
description: Signature edition: Instead of raw text, the agent maintains a knowledge graph of entities and relations (user -works_at-> Acme; Acme -deploys-> Friday). Graph memory supports multi-hop recall ('who works on the Friday deploy?') that flat text search can't, and updates are surgical (change one edge, not a whole summary).
method: Extract (subject, relation, object) triples from observations; upsert into the graph; answer recall queries by graph traversal with embedding fallback.
usage: Define the relation schema for your domain; extract triples on write; traverse on recall.
